project: AI Engineering Lab: the 7 pattern labs
summary: Seven LLM design patterns (RAG, fine-tuning, caching, guardrails, feedback, agent evals, observability), each built as a working, measured Python module on a shared core.

architecture.style: Modular monolith: one FastAPI process, seven pattern modules on a shared core (tracing, providers, embeddings, SQLite), plus one subprocess job runner for training
architecture.summary: Each pattern lives in its own package (backend/lab/p01_rag … p07_observability) with its own router, logic and benchmark. They all lean on lab/core: one LLM client for DeepSeek and Groq, one embedder, one SQLite file, and one tracing helper. Every module wraps its work in tracing.span(...), so every request in every lab becomes a tree of spans that the observability lab (TraceLens) reads back. Two labs reuse others: SignalLoop (feedback) runs RAG questions through the Evidence Atlas pipeline, and TraceLens's demo-traffic button drives RAG, cache, guardrails and agents to create real traces.

deployables.name: FastAPI backend (uvicorn)
deployables.what: Serves every lab's JSON API on 127.0.0.1:8000

deployables.name: Training/eval subprocesses
deployables.what: LoRA training and model evaluation run as separate Python processes so the API stays responsive

deployables.name: CLI experiment scripts
deployables.what: Each lab's benchmark can be run from the terminal (python -m lab.pXX...)

unknowns: No deployment config (Docker, cloud) in the repo: it is a local, single-user lab.
Prefix/KV caching happens inside DeepSeek/Groq servers; the lab only reads the cached-token count they report back.
DeepSeek prices in pricing.json are marked unverified by the author, so cost numbers for DeepSeek are approximate.

groups.name: Entry points
groups.what: How work enters the backend: HTTP routes and background jobs

groups.name: Quality patterns
groups.what: Patterns that make answers more correct: RAG, fine-tuning, agent evals

groups.name: Cost / risk patterns
groups.what: Patterns that make the system cheaper, safer and debuggable: caching, guardrails, observability

groups.name: Feedback loop
groups.what: The flywheel that feeds both axes

groups.name: Shared core
groups.what: Code every lab uses: LLM client, tracing, embeddings, redaction, DB

groups.name: External models & APIs
groups.what: Paid LLM APIs and downloaded open models

nodes.label: FastAPI app + job runner
nodes.what: The single web server. It mounts one router per lab and turns Python errors into clean HTTP errors.
nodes.why: Without it, the frontend would have no way to reach any lab. The error handlers make sure API keys never leak in error messages.
nodes.analogy: A building's reception desk that sends each visitor to the right floor.

nodes.label: App + routers
nodes.what: Creates the FastAPI app and includes each lab's APIRouter (/api/rag, /api/finetune, /api/cache, /api/guard, /api/feedback, /api/agents, /api/traces…).

nodes.label: Error handlers
nodes.what: Converts provider and permission errors into HTTP status codes, scrubbing secrets first.

nodes.label: Shared core
nodes.what: Small helpers every lab imports: config, the one LLM client, tracing, embeddings, PII/secret redaction, SQLite access and the job runner.
nodes.why: Putting these in one place means every lab is traced, redacted and billed the same way. That shared trace schema is what lets evals and observability talk to each other (PDF chapter 7).
responsibilities: Call DeepSeek/Groq with retries and cost tracking
Redact PII and secrets before storage

nodes.label: providers.py (LLM client)
nodes.what: One httpx client for both providers (both speak the OpenAI chat-completions format). Retries 429/5xx with backoff, reads token usage and cached tokens, and computes cost.

nodes.label: tracing.py (spans)
nodes.what: The `with span(...)` context manager. A ContextVar remembers the current span, so spans nest automatically. Content is stored only as length+hash unless capture is turned on.

nodes.label: embeddings.py
nodes.what: Turns text into vectors with MiniLM, or a hash-based fallback if MiniLM can't load. Also provides exact cosine search.

nodes.label: redaction.py
nodes.what: Finds and masks PII (emails, phones, cards with a Luhn check) and scrubs API keys from any text.

nodes.label: db.py
nodes.what: Opens the shared SQLite file (WAL mode). Each lab creates its own tables on first use.

nodes.label: jobs.py (subprocess runner)
nodes.what: Starts training/eval as a separate `python -m ...` process, writes a pid file and log, and allows one job per name.

nodes.label: 01 Evidence Atlas (RAG)
nodes.what: Answers questions over a 15-document investigation corpus with hybrid retrieval, an evidence gate, citations and verification.
nodes.why: Shows the full RAG pipeline from the PDF: incremental indexing, BM25 + vectors fused with RRF, access control, abstention and citation checks. Without retrieval the LLM would guess.
nodes.analogy: A research librarian who fetches the right pages before anyone writes an answer.

nodes.label: index.py (chunk, embed, BM25)
nodes.what: Loads fixture + ingested docs, chunks them, and re-embeds only documents whose content hash changed. Refuses to mix vectors from different embedders.

nodes.label: retrieve.py (hybrid + rerank)
nodes.what: Applies the role-based access filter first, scores with BM25 and dense vectors, fuses with reciprocal rank fusion (k=60), reranks, demotes superseded docs, and fits a word budget.

nodes.label: generate.py (gate, LLM, verify)
nodes.what: Abstains if evidence is too weak; otherwise answers (offline extractive or LLM) and verifies every [S#] citation and quote.

nodes.label: pipeline.py ask()
nodes.what: The end-to-end function: index → retrieve → generate, all inside one rag.ask trace.

nodes.label: evaluate.py (benchmark)
nodes.what: Runs 24 labelled questions and scores retrieval (recall, MRR) separately from answers.

nodes.label: 02 IntentForge (fine-tuning)
nodes.what: Builds a clean dataset, trains a real LoRA adapter on SmolLM2-135M, and compares it with rules, prompting, constrained decoding and an API model.
nodes.why: Demonstrates 'fine-tune second, not first': it measures the prompting baseline, proves the base weights stay frozen, and catches catastrophic forgetting.
responsibilities: Evaluate on test, OOD and general slices

nodes.label: data.py
nodes.what: Synthesises ~700 examples, deliberately corrupts some, then cleans, deduplicates and splits by content hash so near-copies can't leak into test.

nodes.label: schema.py
nodes.what: The strict 7-field Decision model plus business rules and per-field scoring.

nodes.label: model.py (LoRA, constrained decoding)
nodes.what: Loads the base model, attaches LoRA to q/k/v/o projections, runs the explicit training loop, and offers schema-constrained generation.

nodes.label: train.py
nodes.what: One training run: checksums a frozen weight before and after, trains, saves the adapter and metadata.

nodes.label: evaluate.py
nodes.what: Scores each system (rules, base, adapter, constrained, API) on the same held-out slices.

nodes.label: 03 CacheCraft (caching)
nodes.what: An FAQ gateway: exact cache → semantic cache → upstream model, with write-through, TTL, per-user scoping and dependency-based invalidation.
nodes.why: Shows why the similarity threshold is the whole design problem and how to avoid stale or cross-user answers.
responsibilities: Evict on TTL or changed article version
Write misses back to the cache

nodes.label: gateway.py ask()
nodes.what: Serves one request through the cache layers and logs a cache event.

nodes.label: workload.py
nodes.what: A labelled 240-query stream and a threshold sweep that score every hit as correct or false.

nodes.label: 04 TrustBoundary (guardrails)
nodes.what: Triage of untrusted documents into tool actions, protected by input detectors, a schema retry loop, a policy engine, human approval and three-layer SQL least privilege.
nodes.why: Shows layered defence: each layer catches what the others miss (e.g. SELECT * passes the text check but the engine authorizer blocks it).
nodes.analogy: Airport security: bag scan, passport check, and a locked door at the gate.
responsibilities: Allow / require approval / deny per action
Run SQL read-only with an authorizer

nodes.label: detectors.py (input)
nodes.what: Normalises text, finds hidden/base64 instructions, scores injection risk, optionally asks Groq Prompt Guard, and redacts PII.

nodes.label: pipeline.py process()
nodes.what: Runs the whole chain and logs every guardrail trigger.

nodes.label: policy.py
nodes.what: The real boundary: role→tool grants, strict argument schemas, recipient/link rules, taint, and risk tiers that require human approval.

nodes.label: sqlguard.py (3-layer SQL)
nodes.what: Text validator + read-only connection (mode=ro, query_only) + SQLite authorizer callback that denies sensitive columns at execution time.

nodes.label: adversarial.py
nodes.what: Runs a 30-case attack/benign corpus and reports which layer stopped each attack.

nodes.label: 05 SignalLoop (feedback)
nodes.what: A research assistant (built on the RAG lab) that collects ratings, corrections and implicit signals, curates them through review, freezes eval sets and gates releases.
nodes.why: Shows a safe flywheel: raw feedback never goes straight into a dataset, and a release can't be promoted without passing the gate.
responsibilities: Review queue (approval is the only path in)

nodes.label: Collect (ask, rate, signal)
nodes.what: Answers with the production release's RAG config, stores the interaction with a salted user hash, and records feedback with PII redacted.

nodes.label: Curate (queue, review, delete)
nodes.what: Clusters and scores feedback, lets a reviewer approve it into a dataset, and cascades deletions into derived examples and eval sets.

nodes.label: Release gate + promote
nodes.what: Runs candidate vs production on a frozen, hash-checked eval set; promotion raises PermissionError (HTTP 403) without a passing gate.

nodes.label: 06 MissionReplay (agent evals)
nodes.what: A deterministic emergency-dispatch simulator where agents (careful, reckless, LLM) call nine tools; runs are scored on the whole trajectory.
nodes.why: A right final message isn't enough: the evaluator checks tool recall, action precision, argument validity, safety and grounding.
responsibilities: Run agents in a bounded tool loop

nodes.label: sim.py (world + tools)
nodes.what: The simulated world: validates tool arguments, advances the timeline (casualties rise, roads close), enforces budget.

nodes.label: agents.py (loop + recorder)
nodes.what: Three agents. The LLM agent loops until it calls finish or hits max_steps; the Recorder turns each tool call into a span.

nodes.label: evaluate.py (trajectory scoring)
nodes.what: Scores a run's steps and final state; stores runs; optional LLM judge.

nodes.label: 07 TraceLens (observability)
nodes.what: Reads the span table every other lab writes: trace search and waterfall, p50/p95/p99, cost, failures, PSI drift and alerts.
nodes.why: Lets you diagnose a request after the fact. Because evals and production share one span schema, an agent run is just another trace.

nodes.label: metrics.py
nodes.what: All read-side analysis over the spans table, plus alert evaluation.

nodes.label: api.py (playground, demo traffic)
nodes.what: Trace endpoints plus a traced LLM playground and a button that generates real offline traffic through the other labs.

nodes.label: SQLite var/lab.db
nodes.what: One shared database file. Holds spans, rag_docs, cache entries/events, guard log/approvals, feedback tables, agent runs and alerts.

nodes.label: SQLite var/p04/analytics.db
nodes.what: A seeded sample business database (customers, orders, a fake secret) that the SQL guard queries read-only.

nodes.label: Files: data/ + var/
nodes.what: Committed fixtures (corpus, benchmarks, KB, adversarial cases, scenarios) and runtime artefacts (datasets, adapters, eval results, job logs).

nodes.label: DeepSeek API
nodes.what: OpenAI-compatible chat API at api.deepseek.com. Used only when DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set and offline mode is off.

nodes.label: Groq API
nodes.what: OpenAI-compatible chat API (gpt-oss models and Llama Prompt Guard). Used only when GROQ_API_KEY is set.

nodes.label: Local HF models
nodes.what: Downloaded open models run on CPU: MiniLM embeddings, the ms-marco cross-encoder, and SmolLM2-135M for LoRA. Need the ML extras installed.

links.label: redact_pii before the model sees text
run_benchmark on frozen set (baseline vs candidate)

flows.name: RAG question (Evidence Atlas)
flows.trigger: User asks a question in Evidence Atlas
flows.description: Shows the full retrieve → gate → generate → verify chain and how each stage limits what the next can do.

steps.text: The router validates the request with pydantic (question length, k, strategy) and calls ask(). A root span rag.ask starts, so everything below is one trace.
get_index syncs the corpus: only documents whose hash changed are re-chunked and re-embedded. This is the PDF's incremental indexing.
Access control runs first: chunks the role can't see are excluded before ranking, so they can never reach the prompt.
The query is embedded and compared with every chunk vector (exact numpy scan). BM25 scores are computed in parallel for exact IDs like 'POL-001-v3'.

Reciprocal rank fusion merges the two lists (1/(60+rank)), then a reranker reorders, superseded docs are halved, and chunks are added until the word budget. The top-k become the only knowledge the model will see.
The evidence gate checks the hits really cover the question. If not, the system abstains instead of guessing (graceful degradation).
With LLM on, the numbered sources and the question are sent to DeepSeek/Groq. The call becomes an llm span with real tokens and cost.
verify() checks every [S#] points to a real passage and that quotes and numbers appear in the cited text. Invalid citations mark the span as failed.
The answer, hits, citations, verification and trace_id go back. The trace_id lets you open the same request in TraceLens.
steps.data: JSON {answer, abstained, hits, citations, verification, trace_id}

flows.name: Cached FAQ request (CacheCraft)
flows.trigger: A user asks an FAQ question
flows.description: Exact → semantic → upstream, with invalidation checks before anything is served and write-through on a miss.

steps.text: The question is classified as global, per-user or volatile. Volatile questions (live status) bypass the cache entirely.
Candidates are loaded only within the same config fingerprint and scope key. Per-user scoping is what stops one user's balance being served to another.
steps.data: SELECT cache_entries WHERE namespace, fingerprint, scope_key

steps.text: Entries whose TTL expired, or whose source article version changed, are evicted before they can be served. This is dependency-based invalidation.
No exact hit? The question is embedded and compared with cached questions. A hit needs similarity ≥ threshold; just below it is logged as a 'rejected match'.
On a miss, the relevant FAQ articles are routed in as context and the model is called. Article versions are kept as dependencies.
Write-through: the new answer, its embedding and dependencies are stored so the next similar question is a hit.
The response says hit_exact / hit_semantic / miss / bypass, with similarity, latency and cost avoided.

flows.name: Untrusted document → actions (TrustBoundary)
flows.trigger: Analyst submits an email/document for triage
flows.description: Layered guardrails: detect, plan with retries, enforce policy per action, then require humans for risky actions.

steps.text: The document enters with a role (analyst, etc.). A guard.process root span starts.
Input guardrails: normalise Unicode, find hidden or base64 instructions, score injection risk, redact PII.
If risk ≥ the block threshold, the request is blocked before any model call. Between flag and block thresholds the input is 'tainted' and side effects need approval.
The planner proposes actions as JSON. Invalid output is retried up to 2 times with the error fed back, then the system fails closed and executes nothing.
Every proposed action passes the policy engine: is this tool granted to this role, are the arguments valid, is it high risk?
steps.data: action + role + taint → allow | approval | deny

steps.text: Allowed SQL runs on a read-only connection with an authorizer that denies sensitive columns while the query executes.
Risky actions (outbound email, P1 tickets, exports) are queued for human approval instead of running. Friction by design.
Output guardrails redact PII from the summary and defang hostile links, then return per-action decisions.

flows.name: Agent mission scored on trajectory (MissionReplay)
flows.trigger: User runs an agent on a scenario
flows.description: A bounded tool-use loop where every tool call is a span, then the whole trajectory is scored.

steps.text: The route checks the scenario exists and that a provider is configured for the LLM agent.
run() creates a fresh simulator and opens an agent.run root span.
Each turn the model gets the conversation plus nine tool schemas. The loop ends when it calls finish, hits max_steps, or replies twice without a tool.
Each tool call is validated and executed in the simulated world, which keeps changing (casualties rise, roads close). The Recorder wraps it in a tool span.
If the model emits invalid JSON tool arguments, the error is recorded and sent back so it can retry; 3 in a row aborts.
evaluate() scores the trajectory, not the final message: required-call recall, action precision, argument validity, safety violations, grounding and efficiency.
The run, its trace_id and evaluation are stored so TraceLens can show the same run as a span tree.

flows.name: Feedback → gated release (SignalLoop)
flows.trigger: A user rates an answer; later a reviewer gates a new release
flows.description: The flywheel: collect, curate by review, freeze an eval set, and promote only when the gate passes.

steps.text: Questions are answered by the RAG pipeline using the production release's config.
The interaction is stored with a salted user hash, never the raw user id. Feedback text is PII-redacted.
A reviewer approves feedback into a dataset. Injection-like corrections and training use without consent are refused.
The gate re-checks the frozen set's hash, then runs baseline and candidate on it.
Promotion without a passing gate raises PermissionError, which the app turns into HTTP 403.

flows.name: LoRA training job (IntentForge)
flows.description: Training runs as a separate process so the API stays responsive; the UI polls a status file.

steps.text: The route builds CLI args and asks the job runner to spawn training. A second concurrent run is refused with 409.
A new Python process starts; the API returns immediately with the run_id.
The base model loads, a frozen weight is checksummed, and LoRA matrices are attached to the attention projections.
Progress is written to status.json every few steps (the UI polls /runs). At the end the adapter and proof the base didn't change are saved.
